L87: # Wheel distribution format【81†¶】
L88: 
L89: This page specifies the wheel format for Python packages.
L90: A wheel is a ZIP-format archive with a specially formatted file name and the `.whl` extension. It contains a single distribution nearly as it would be installed according to PEP 376 with a particular installation scheme. Although a specialized installer is recommended, a wheel file may be installed by simply unpacking into site-packages with the standard ‘unzip’ tool while preserving enough information to spread its contents out onto their final paths at any later time.
L91: ## Details【82†¶】
L92: ### Installing a wheel ‘distribution-1.0-py32-none-any.whl’【83†¶】
L93: 
L94: Wheel installation notionally consists of two phases:
L95: 
L96:   * Unpack.
L97: 
L98:     1. Parse `distribution-1.0.dist-info/WHEEL`.
L99: 
L100:     2. Check that installer is compatible with Wheel-Version. Warn if minor version is greater, abort if major version is greater.
L101: 
L102:     3. If Root-Is-Purelib == ‘true’, unpack archive into purelib (site-packages).
L103: 
L104:     4. Else unpack archive into platlib (site-packages).
L105: 
L106:   * Spread.
L107:     1. Unpacked archive includes `distribution-1.0.dist-info/` and (if there is data) `distribution-1.0.data/`.
L108: 
L109:     2. Move each subtree of `distribution-1.0.data/` onto its destination path. Each subdirectory of `distribution-1.0.data/` is a key into a dict of destination directories, such as `distribution-1.0.data/(purelib|platlib|headers|scripts|data)`. These subdirectories are 【84†installation paths defined by sysconfig†docs.python.org】.
L110:     3. If applicable, update scripts starting with `#!python` to point to the correct interpreter.
L111: 
L112:     4. Update `distribution-1.0.dist-info/RECORD` with the installed paths.
L113: 
L114:     5. Remove empty `distribution-1.0.data` directory.
L115: 
L116:     6. Compile any installed .py to .pyc. (Uninstallers should be smart enough to remove .pyc even if it is not mentioned in RECORD.)
L117: #### Recommended installer features【85†¶】
L118: 
L119: Rewrite `#!python`.
L120: 
L121: 
L122: In wheel, scripts are packaged in `{distribution}-{version}.data/scripts/`. If the first line of a file in `scripts/` starts with exactly `b'#!python'`, rewrite to point to the correct interpreter. Unix installers may need to add the +x bit to these files if the archive was created on Windows.
L123: 
L124: The `b'#!pythonw'` convention is allowed. `b'#!pythonw'` indicates a GUI script instead of a console script.
L125: 
L126: Generate script wrappers.
L127: In wheel, scripts packaged on Unix systems will certainly not have accompanying .exe wrappers. Windows installers may want to add them during install.
L128: #### Recommended archiver features【86†¶】
L129: 
L130: Place `.dist-info` at the end of the archive.
L131: 
L132: 
L133: Archivers are encouraged to place the `.dist-info` files physically at the end of the archive. This enables some potentially interesting ZIP tricks including the ability to amend the metadata without rewriting the entire archive.
L134: 
L135: ### File Format【87†¶】
L136: #### File name convention【88†¶】
L137: 
L138: The wheel filename is `{distribution}-{version}(-{build tag})?-{python tag}-{abi tag}-{platform tag}.whl`.
L139: 
L140: distribution
L141: 
L142: 
L143: Distribution name, e.g. ‘django’, ‘pyramid’.
L144: 
L145: version
L146: 
L147: 
L148: Distribution version, e.g. 1.0.
L149: 
L150: build tag
L151: Optional build number. Must start with a digit. Acts as a tie-breaker if two wheel file names are the same in all other respects (i.e. name, version, and other tags). Sort as an empty tuple if unspecified, else sort as a two-item tuple with the first item being the initial digits as an `int`, and the second item being the remainder of the tag as a `str`.
L152: A common use-case for build numbers is rebuilding a binary distribution due to a change in the build environment, like when using the manylinux image to build distributions using pre-release CPython versions.
L153: 
L154: Warning
L155: 
L156: Build numbers are not a part of the distribution version and thus are difficult to reference externally, especially so outside the Python ecosystem of tools and standards. A common case where a distribution would need to referenced externally is when resolving a security vulnerability.
L157: Due to this limitation, new distributions which need to be referenced externally should not use build numbers when building the new distribution. Instead a new distribution version should be created for such cases.
L158: 
L159: language implementation and version tag
L160: 
L161: 
L162: E.g. ‘py27’, ‘py2’, ‘py3’.
L163: 
L164: abi tag
L165: 
L166: 
L167: E.g. ‘cp33m’, ‘abi3’, ‘none’.
L168: 
L169: platform tag
L170: 
L171: 
L172: E.g. ‘linux_x86_64’, ‘any’.
L173: For example, `distribution-1.0-1-py27-none-any.whl` is the first build of a package called ‘distribution’, and is compatible with Python 2.7 (any Python 2.7 implementation), with no ABI (pure Python), on any CPU architecture.
L174: 
L175: The last three components of the filename before the extension are called “compatibility tags.” The compatibility tags express the package’s basic interpreter requirements and are detailed in PEP 425.
L176: #### Escaping and Unicode【89†¶】
L177: 
L178: As the components of the filename are separated by a dash (`-`, HYPHEN-MINUS), this character cannot appear within any component. This is handled as follows:
L179:   * In distribution names, any run of `-_.` characters (HYPHEN-MINUS, LOW LINE and FULL STOP) should be replaced with `_` (LOW LINE), and uppercase characters should be replaced with corresponding lowercase ones. This is equivalent to regular 【90†name normalization】 followed by replacing `-` with `_`. Tools consuming wheels must be prepared to accept `.` (FULL STOP) and uppercase letters, however, as these were allowed by an earlier version of this specification.
L180:   * Version numbers should be normalised according to the 【91†Version specifier specification】. Normalised version numbers cannot contain `-`.
L181: 
L182:   * The remaining components may not contain `-` characters, so no escaping is necessary.
L183: 
L184: Tools producing wheels should verify that the filename components do not contain `-`, as the resulting file may not be processed correctly if they do.
L185: The archive filename is Unicode. It will be some time before the tools are updated to support non-ASCII filenames, but they are supported in this specification.
L186: 
L187: The filenames inside the archive are encoded as UTF-8. Although some ZIP clients in common use do not properly display UTF-8 filenames, the encoding is supported by both the ZIP specification and Python’s `zipfile`.
L188: #### File contents【92†¶】
L189: 
L190: The contents of a wheel file, where {distribution} is replaced with the 【90†normalized name】 of the package, e.g. `beaglevote` and {version} is replaced with its 【93†normalized version】, e.g. `1.0.0`, (with dash/`-` characters replaced with underscore/`_` characters in both fields) consist of:
L191: 
L192:   1. `/`, the root of the archive, contains all files to be installed in `purelib` or `platlib` as specified in `WHEEL`. `purelib` and `platlib` are usually both `site-packages`.
L193:   2. `{distribution}-{version}.dist-info/` contains metadata.
L194: 
L195:   3. `distribution-version.dist-info/licenses/` contains license files.
L196: 
L197:   4. `{distribution}-{version}.data/` contains one subdirectory for each non-empty install scheme key not already covered, where the subdirectory name is an index into a dictionary of install paths (e.g. `data`, `scripts`, `headers`, `purelib`, `platlib`).
L198:   5. Python scripts must appear in `scripts` and begin with exactly `b'#!python'` in order to enjoy script wrapper generation and `#!python` rewriting at install time. They may have any or no extension. The `scripts` directory may only contain regular files.
L199: 
L200:   6. `{distribution}-{version}.dist-info/METADATA` is Metadata version 1.1 or greater format metadata.
L201:   7. `{distribution}-{version}.dist-info/WHEEL` is metadata about the archive itself in the same basic key: value format:
L202: 
L203:     Wheel-Version: 1.0
L204:     Generator: bdist_wheel 1.0
L205:     Root-Is-Purelib: true
L206:     Tag: py2-none-any
L207:     Tag: py3-none-any
L208:     Build: 1
L209: 
L210: 
L211:   8. `Wheel-Version` is the version number of the Wheel specification.
L212: 
L213:   9. `Generator` is the name and optionally the version of the software that produced the archive.
L214:   10. `Root-Is-Purelib` is true if the top level directory of the archive should be installed into purelib; otherwise the root should be installed into platlib.
L215: 
L216:   11. `Tag` is the wheel’s expanded compatibility tags; in the example the filename would contain `py2.py3-none-any`.
L217: 
L218:   12. `Build` is the build number and is omitted if there is no build number.
L219:   13. A wheel installer should warn if Wheel-Version is greater than the version it supports, and must fail if Wheel-Version has a greater major version than the version it supports.
L220: 
L221:   14. Wheel, being an installation format that is intended to work across multiple versions of Python, does not generally include .pyc files.
L222: 
L223:   15. Wheel does not contain setup.py or setup.cfg.
L224: This version of the wheel specification is based on the distutils install schemes and does not define how to install files to other locations. The layout offers a superset of the functionality provided by the existing wininst and egg binary formats.
L225: ##### The .dist-info directory【94†¶】
L226: 
L227:   1. Wheel .dist-info directories include at a minimum METADATA, WHEEL, and RECORD.
L228: 
L229:   2. METADATA is the package metadata, the same format as PKG-INFO as found at the root of sdists.
L230: 
L231:   3. WHEEL is the wheel metadata specific to a build of the package.
L232:   4. RECORD is a list of (almost) all the files in the wheel and their secure hashes. Unlike PEP 376, every file except RECORD, which cannot contain a hash of itself, must include its hash. The hash algorithm must be sha256 or better; specifically, md5 and sha1 are not permitted.
L233: 
L234:   5. PEP 376’s INSTALLER and REQUESTED are not included in the archive.
L235:   6. RECORD.jws and RECORD.p7s are deprecated. Where they are still used, neither RECORD.jws nor RECORD.p7s are mentioned in RECORD. Build backends and other tools must not add them to wheels anymore, installers should be aware that these files may still be part of some wheels.
L236:   7. During extraction, wheel installers verify all the hashes in RECORD against the file contents. Apart from RECORD, RECORD.jws and RECORD.p7s, installation will fail if any file in the archive is not both mentioned and correctly hashed in RECORD.
L237: ##### Subdirectories in `.dist-info/`【95†¶】
L238: 
L239: Subdirectories under `.dist-info/` are reserved for future use. The following subdirectory names under `.dist-info/` are reserved for specific usage:
L240: 
L241: Subdirectory name  | PEP / Standard
L242: --- | ---
L243: `licenses`  | 【96†PEP 639†peps.python.org】
L244: `license_files`  | 【96†PEP 639†peps.python.org】
L245: `LICENSES`  | 【97†REUSE licensing framework†reuse.software】
L246: `sboms`  | 【98†PEP 770†peps.python.org】
L247: ##### The `.dist-info/licenses/` directory【99†¶】
L248: 
L249: If the metadata version is 2.4 or greater and one or more `License-File` fields is specified, the `.dist-info/` directory MUST contain a `licenses/` subdirectory, which MUST contain the files listed in the `License-File` fields in the `METADATA` file at their respective paths relative to the `licenses/` directory.
L250: ##### The `.dist-info/sboms/` directory【100†¶】
L251: 
L252: All files contained within the `.dist-info/sboms/` directory MUST be Software Bill-of-Materials (SBOM) files that describe software contained within the distribution archive.
L253: ##### The .data directory【101†¶】
L254: 
L255: Any file that is not normally installed inside site-packages goes into the .data directory, named as the .dist-info directory but with the .data/ extension:
L256: 
L257:     distribution-1.0.dist-info/
L258: 
L259:     distribution-1.0.data/
L260: 
L261: 
L262: The .data directory contains subdirectories with the scripts, headers, documentation and so forth from the distribution. During installation the contents of these subdirectories are moved onto their destination paths.
L263: 
L264: ## FAQ【102†¶】
L265: ### Wheel defines a .data directory. Should I put all my data there?【103†¶】
L266: 
L267: > This specification does not have an opinion on how you should organize your code. The .data directory is just a place for any files that are not normally installed inside `site-packages` or on the PYTHONPATH. In other words, you may continue to use `pkgutil.get_data(package, resource)` even though those files will usually not be distributed in wheel’s `.data` directory.
L268: ### What’s the deal with “purelib” vs. “platlib”?【104†¶】
L269: > Wheel preserves the “purelib” vs. “platlib” distinction, which is significant on some platforms. For example, Fedora installs pure Python packages to ‘/usr/lib/pythonX.Y/site-packages’ and platform dependent packages to ‘/usr/lib64/pythonX.Y/site-packages’.
L270: >
L271: > A wheel with “Root-Is-Purelib: false” with all its files in `{name}-{version}.data/purelib` is equivalent to a wheel with “Root-Is-Purelib: true” with those same files in the root, and it is legal to have files in both the “purelib” and “platlib” categories.
L272: >
L273: > In practice a wheel should have only one of “purelib” or “platlib” depending on whether it is pure Python or not and those files should be at the root with the appropriate setting given for “Root-is-purelib”.
L274: ### Is it possible to import Python code directly from a wheel file?【105†¶】
L275: > Technically, due to the combination of supporting installation via simple extraction and using an archive format that is compatible with `zipimport`, a subset of wheel files do support being placed directly on `sys.path`. However, while this behaviour is a natural consequence of the format design, actually relying on it is generally discouraged.
L276: >
L277: > Firstly, wheel is designed primarily as a distribution format, so skipping the installation step also means deliberately avoiding any reliance on features that assume full installation (such as being able to use standard tools like `pip` and `virtualenv` to capture and manage dependencies in a way that can be properly tracked for auditing and security update purposes, or integrating fully with the standard build machinery for C extensions by publishing header files in the appropriate place).
L278: >
L279: > Secondly, while some Python software is written to support running directly from a zip archive, it is still common for code to be written assuming it has been fully installed. When that assumption is broken by trying to run the software from a zip archive, the failures can often be obscure and hard to diagnose (especially when they occur in third party libraries).
L280: The two most common sources of problems with this are the fact that importing C extensions from a zip archive is not supported by CPython (since doing so is not supported directly by the dynamic loading machinery on any platform) and that when running from a zip archive the `__file__` attribute no longer refers to an ordinary filesystem path, but to a combination path that includes both the location of the zip archive on the filesystem and the relative path to the module inside the archive.
L281: Even when software correctly uses the abstract resource APIs internally, interfacing with external components may still require the availability of an actual on-disk file.
L282: >
L283: > Like metaclasses, monkeypatching and metapath importers, if you’re not already sure you need to take advantage of this feature, you almost certainly don’t need it. If you do decide to use it anyway, be aware that many projects will require a failure to be reproduced with a fully installed package before accepting it as a genuine bug.
L284: ## History【106†¶】
L285: 
L286:   * February 2013: This specification was approved through 【107†PEP 427†peps.python.org】.
L287: 
L288:   * February 2021: The rules on escaping in wheel filenames were revised, to bring them into line with what popular tools actually do.
L289: 
L290:   * December 2024: Clarified that the `scripts` folder should only contain regular files (the expected behaviour of consuming tools when encountering symlinks or subdirectories in this folder is not formally defined, and hence may vary between tools).
L291:   * December 2024: The `.dist-info/licenses/` directory was specified through 【96†PEP 639†peps.python.org】.
L292: 
L293:   * January 2025: Clarified that name and version needs to be normalized for `.dist-info` and `.data` directories.
L294: 
L295:   * January 2026: Deprecate RECORD.jws and RECORD.p7s 【108†PEP 815†peps.python.org】.
L296: ## Appendix【109†¶】
L297: 
L298: Example urlsafe-base64-nopad implementation:
L299: 
L300:     # urlsafe-base64-nopad for Python 3
L301:     import base64
L302: 
L303:     def urlsafe_b64encode_nopad(data):
L304:         return base64.urlsafe_b64encode(data).rstrip(b'=')
L305: 
L306:     def urlsafe_b64decode_nopad(data):
L307:         pad = b'=' * (4 - (len(data) & 3))
L308:         return base64.urlsafe_b64decode(data + pad)
